teaching: Tawhid (monotheism) is the most exalted of all Islamic sciences and surpasses all other scholarly discourses in greatness.
God (Mubdi' Subhanahu) is the Originator who brought existence from nothingness; this is distinct from a creator (Khaliq) who reshapes pre-existing material.
Four things belong exclusively to God: worship (ibadat/sajdah), sovereignty (mulk), sustenance (rizq), and command (amr).

Prostration (sajdah) is permissible only before God; the seven limbs touching the ground defines a true prostration, and any bow not meeting this definition is merely a gesture of respect, not sajdah.
The command (amr) descends through a cosmic hierarchy: from God to the First Intellect, through the ten intellects, to the Imam of the era, and then through the da'i, ma'dhun, and mukasir.
True Tawhid does not merely mean believing God is one (wahid) among countable things; it means recognising Him as absolutely unique (ahad), beyond all counting and enumeration.

According to Sayyidna Muayyad al-Din, Tawhid is defined as the gnosis of all spiritual and physical ranks (hudud), high and low, and the acknowledgment that each rank is unique in its station with no partner.
The ranks in the da'wah hierarchy are fixed by divine command (nass-e-juz'i) from above; no human authority can reassign someone from one rank to another.
Tanzih (transcendence) means God is purified from all attributes; the ninety-nine divine names properly apply to created beings who manifest those qualities, not to God Himself.

The ninety-nine names of God are properly attributed to the First Intellect ('Aql-e-Awwal), God's most exalted servant; the name of the divine essence (ism al-dhat) such as 'Rahman' belongs to God alone.
Tajrid (abstraction) means stripping the attribute of divinity (ilahiyyah) away from everything except God; the power to bring existence from nothingness belongs to God alone.
God created countless luminous essences in the spiritual world simultaneously, in a uniform state, in a single stroke (ba-qat'in wahidah), in a form like the letter alif (qamat-e-alifiyyah).

The First Intellect achieved primacy by recognising without any teacher that neither he nor other essences could create themselves, but that a third being created all of them — this acknowledgment was the greatest event in the spiritual world.
When the First Intellect acknowledged God, divine support (ta'id) flowed upon him, increasing his luminosity; this self-enjoyment (masarrat) caused the two rising beings (munba'ithayn) to notice him.

Two beings arose from the assembled essences: the first munba'ith sought the inner cause (batin) of the First Intellect's luminosity, while the second munba'ith was occupied with the outward appearance (mazhariyyah); the one focused on inner reality advanced further.
The second munba'ith fell into the illusion of equality (wahm-e-masawat), thinking himself equal to the first munba'ith; this was his error and caused him to fall behind.
The First Intellect became a veil (hijab) between God (Mubdi' Subhanahu) and all other creation; no one can directly reach or comprehend God — one can only affirm His existence.
key_terms: tafakkaru fi 'l-makhluq wa la tafakkaru fi 'l-khaliq

teaching: The prophetic tradition states: 'Reflect on the creation, and do not reflect on the Creator' — one should not attempt to mentally grasp God Himself.
Seven intellects advanced after the First Intellect before the second munba'ith finally repented, giving a total of ten intellects; the second munba'ith became the Tenth Intellect.
The Tenth Intellect is the Adam of the spiritual world; just as Adam in the physical world erred and repented, the Tenth Intellect erred (illusion of equality) and repented (taba wa anaba).

After the Tenth Intellect repented, the remaining disobedient essences split into four groups: those who repented with him (tabu bi-tawbatihi, ~15%), those who answered the call when invited (labbu 'l-nida', ~30%), those who hesitated for an eyeblink (kallamam), and those who persisted in refusal (la nasma'u wa la nuti').
The Mustaqarr Imams (such as those from Mawlana Hasan onwards) are from the group of kallamam — those who hesitated for an eyeblink before accepting in the spiritual world.

Iblis and Shaytan are distinct: Iblis spoke the word of refusal out of ignorance, while Shaytan was the instigator (muharrik) who incited others not to accept; in the era of Muhammad, the first caliph corresponds to Iblis and the second to Shaytan.

When the disobedient essences were expelled from the spiritual world, darkness (zulmat) spread in them in three stages, producing three physical dimensions — length, width, and depth — rendering them unfit to remain in the spiritual world.

When the command 'Ahbitu' (Descend!) was given, the essences were divided into three groups at the moment of expulsion: the regretful (nadim wa mustaghfir), the insistent and arrogant (musirr wa mustakbir), and the doubtful and bewildered (shakk wa mutahayyir).

The stars and heavens were formed from the nadimin (the regretful); the hard core of the earth and what is below it from the musirr wa mustakbir; and the four spheres of fire, air, water, and earth from the shakk wa mutahayyirin.

The leaven (khamir) of regret from the nadimin was deposited in the Spiritual Kaaba (Ka'bah al-Ruhani / ta'ud / markaz / qalb / 'alam-e-hayat); the rational souls (nufus-e-natiqah) of believers are attached to the Pillar of Light ('Amud al-Nur) next to it.

The Prophet's hadith that 'After me my community will be divided into 73 sects' refers to the 70 cosmic groups (15 nadimin + 20 mutahayyirin + 35 musirrin) plus one representative cream drawn from each of the three divisions, totaling 73; the one sect that attains salvation is the highest portion of the nadimin.
key_terms: sataftariqu ba'di ummati thalathan wa sab'ina firqah

teaching: The Tenth Intellect ('Aql-e-'Ashir) is the governor (mudabbir) and administrator of the entire physical world, and is our Khaliq (Creator); he must reform those who fell due to the spiritual world's error because the divine principle is 'man kasara 'azmuhu fa-'alayhi jabruhu' (he who breaks a bone must mend it).

The spiritual world extends from the First Intellect to the Tenth Intellect; below that is the world of life ('alam-e-hayat), then the world of Jibra'il ('alam-e-jibra'il / 'alam-e-jirmani), then the physical world ('alam-e-jism) below the moon.
The Hadith 'Man 'arafa nafsahu faqad 'arafa rabbahu' (Whoever knows his own self has known his Lord) means that self-knowledge is the path to recognising the divine ranks and advancing spiritually.

Adam (the first man) with twelve naqibs and twenty-seven hujjahs remained in the world of life at the moment of expulsion, forming the primordial structure of 28 — a pattern that reflects the Imam's cabinet in every era.
The Sulaymanis are from the nadimin group; their attachment to the rational soul (nafs-e-natiqah) deposited in the Spiritual Kaaba is the reason they are born as Sulaymanis across generations.

The Tenth Intellect planned three things for the salvation of fallen essences: salvation only through the human form (ashraf al-makhluqat), the mechanism of laghut and nasut (imamate and the Imam's body), and the creation of animal forms as punishment-cages for those who descend.

Human beings uniquely possess natiqah (the faculty of reason linked to guardianship/walayah); ordinary humans have only nutq (speech/intellect) but natiqah can only be obtained by entering the circle of walayah and accepting the Imam of the time.

The spiritual hierarchy of ranks of progress in the da'wah begins at mustajib, then mu'min (ten ranks), then kashif, then ma'dhun-e-mahdud, ma'dhun-e-mutlaq, da'i, tali-e-bab, hujjat, bab, and up through babiyyah to imamah.
The walayah (guardianship/love) of Amir al-Muminin Ali is the soul of the entire religion; without it, no prayer, fast, hajj, zakat, or any pillar of the Da'a'im al-Islam is complete.
Every Muslim is not a mu'min, but every mu'min is necessarily a Muslim — the circle of iman (faith) is a smaller circle within the larger circle of Islam.
Death (mawt) is a certain reality (al-mawtu haqqun); for the mu'min it is sweet like a fragrance (rayhanu 'l-mawt), while for the unbeliever it is terrible.

After death, the body's residue undergoes chemical changes, passes through a 720-year cycle in the sphere of constellations (falak-e-buruj), then 280 years in the mineral-plant-animal world, totaling 1000 years before returning to a new human form.

The residue of a deceased mu'min travels first to the qalb-e-jazirah (heart of the island) in Bombay (the current spiritual center), then to the miqat, then to the falak-e-buruj where it is refined over 720 years.

There are three types of souls (nafs) given to a mu'min: nawiyah (vegetative power), hissiyyah (sensory power), and natiqah (rational soul); the natiqah is received at the spiritual birth when the covenant ('ahd) is taken.

The verse 'maraj al-baḥrayni yaltaqiyan' (He released the two seas, meeting) refers to the chains of Prophethood and Imamate meeting at the marriage of Ali and Fatimah; the pearl and coral (lu'lu' wa marjan) are Hasan and Husayn.

The Prophet's hadith states: 'Hasan and Husayn are two rightful Imams, whether they rise or sit, and their father is better than both of them' — Hasan 'sat' (made a truce) and Husayn 'rose' (in Karbala); Ali is superior to both as Wasi.

The heart's scarlet blood (dam-e-sarwizi) circulates to produce innate heat (hararat-e-gharizi), which is our life force (jan) in a gaseous form; this gaseous state is closer to the spiritual world and is the next stage of bodily progress toward the spiritual.
The Tenth Intellect's plan for adorning the world began with making the all-encompassing sphere (falak-e-muhit) revolve, initiating the cycle of day and night, months and years.

Each of the seven planets has a special governor (mudabbir) whose spiritual center (markaz) is the ruling intelligence of that sphere; the surface of a planet is its outward shell (sadaf) while the center is its ruhaniyyah (spirituality).

The first planetary leadership (sardari) was given to Saturn (Zuhal), a harsh star counted among the two inauspicious ones (nahsayn); the two auspicious stars (sa'dayn) are Venus (Zahra) and Jupiter (Mushtari); the two luminaries (nayyirayn) are the moon and sun; Mercury ('Utarid) is the scribe of the sphere (munshi-e-falak).

The dawr of Saturn lasted 7000 years: 1000 years of Saturn alone (world covered in ice), then Saturn joined by each subsequent planet in successive millennia; each planet's influence shaped what was created in the mineral, plant, and animal kingdoms during its era.

After 42,000 years of planetary eras, the era of the Moon began; in the final 7000-year lunar period, the leavens (khamir/sulale) for human creation were prepared, and humans were manifested in the last part of that period.

In the beginning of a kawr (great cosmic cycle), the first humans were not born from a mother's womb but emerged from pits (khudda) in the earth shaped like a womb; the most noble khudda were at the Ka'ba, Madinah, Masjid al-Aqsa, and other sacred sites.

The first batch of humans created from the pits were all male (mudhakkar); the second batch, from the remaining water in the same pits, were female; women are considered more delicate (nazuk) because they were created from leftover water — reflected in the Quranic verse 'al-rijalu qawwamuna 'ala al-nisa'.

At the Ka'ba, 28 men and then 28 women were created from pits; the first man (Kayumarth-e-A'zam / Jussa-e-Ibda'iyyah) was accompanied by 27 others (twelve da'is of one kind, twelve of another, one mukasir, one ma'dhun, one Bab al-Abwab) — a structure of 28 replicated with every Imam's cabinet.

All of human history begins with a single lineage from the first Imam (Kayumarth-e-A'zam): 'wahidan ba'da wahid, waladan min walad ila yawm al-qiyamah' (one after another, son from son, until the Day of Resurrection).
A dawr (era) consists of seven periods of kashf (500,000 years total) and seven periods of sitr (49,000 years total); seven such alternating cycles make one dawr of approximately 400,000 years.

One Kawr-e-A'zam (great cosmic cycle) = 4 lakh (400,000) dawrs of 400,000 years each = 16,000 crore years; one Mawr-e-A'zam = 4 lakh Kawrs; the Imam Zayn al-'Abidin told Umm al-Da'i that one Mawr-e-A'zam has fully passed and of the second, 399 kawrs have passed — we are in the last sitr of the first dawr of the 400th kawr.

Every period of dawr-e-kashf (unveiling) begins with the Imam present and the da'wah fully active; dawr-e-sitr (concealment) lasts 7,000 years, during which the Imam is hidden and du'at, hujjat, and mansub operate in their place — this is analogous to night following day.

The beginning of dawr-e-sitr is introduced by a period of dawr-e-fitrat (period of spiritual laxity) lasting 3,000 years, during which people abandon the hudud for occult practitioners ('amils) and sciences like palmistry, raml, and jafr.
The Qaim al-Muntazar (the awaited Qaim) will take reckoning for 400,000 years of deeds; his arrival will be sudden (baghtatan) unlike the Qaim whose coming is a known day (yawm-e-ma'lum).

The qiyamat (resurrection) has four grades: qiyamat-e-saghira (of sitr), qiyamat-e-wusta (of dawr), qiyamat-e-kubra (of kawr), and qiyamat-e-uzma (of mawr); each is presided over by a Qaim of increasing rank.

The emotional bonds people feel in this life (love for siblings, attraction between husband and wife, etc.) originate in the gazes ('nazrein') that were fixed in the 'alam-e-hayat (world of life) before descent into the physical world.

The Prophet is the spiritual sun (aftab) of the era of Muhammad: the Quran uses 'sirajan wahhajan' for the physical sun and 'sirajan munira' for the Prophet, showing they are parallel — after the Prophet, the Imam of every era takes the rank of the spiritual sun.

Ali is the spiritual moon (mahtab) of the da'wah: just as the moon has no independent light but receives it from the sun, Ali received knowledge from the Prophet through the bab (door); 'the Prophet opened for me the doors of knowledge and from every door a thousand other doors were opened for me.'

The exoteric interpretation (ta'wil) of 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' is that 'Bi-ism' means 'in the name of', and the greatest name (ism) of God is the being of the First Intellect; we begin in the name of God through the First Intellect as the named intermediary.

The verse 'dhalik al-kitab la rayba fih' uses the distal demonstrative 'dhalik' (that) rather than 'hadha' (this) because the Kitab al-Natiq (Speaking Book) it refers to is Ali ibn Abi Talib, who lived 1400 years ago and is therefore 'that' book, not 'this' one — the Quran on paper is the silent book (Kitab al-Samit), and Ali is the speaking book (Kitab al-Natiq).
Ali ibn Abi Talib declared: 'Hadha kitabullah al-samit wa ana kitabullah al-natiq' (This is the silent Book of Allah, and I am the speaking Book of Allah) — proving his status as the living Quran.

The obligatory (fardh) prayers are 17 raka'ts daily: Fajr 2, Zuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4; the five prayer times are attributed (mansulat) to five prophets: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and the Prophet Muhammad.

At the times of the five obligatory prayers, special gates (issuing gates / manfas) open in the falak-e-muhit through which spiritual forms (suwarat) descend from 'alam al-arwah; these suwarat give the prayer its spiritual validity and reward.

The Zuhr prayer is attributed to the Prophet Muhammad because his sunlight of prophethood shone at its brightest like the midday sun; its four raka'ts correspond to the four letters Mim, Ha, Mim, Dal of Muhammad.

The Asr prayer is attributed to Qaim (salawatullah 'alayh) because 'asr' means both 'era' and 'essence/juice' — the Qaim is the essence of the world; the four letters of Qaim match the four raka'ts, and after the Qaim comes no new shari'ah.

The Maghrib prayer is attributed to Ali (salawatullah 'alayh); its three raka'ts correspond to the three letters of 'Ali; the short duration of Maghrib time mirrors the brief caliphate of Ali in the physical world.

The Isha prayer is attributed to the Imam of each era during the long period of sitr (concealment) from Tayyib until today; its long time window mirrors the extended dark night of sitr that began with Adam's era.

The Fajr prayer will be attributed to Mahdi (salawatullah 'alayh) whose coming will be sudden (baghtatan) like the dawn spreading suddenly; the four letters of Mahdi (M-H-D) parallel the four letters of Muhammad.

Wearing items made of iron, brass, or other falling (descending) materials on one's body during prayer makes the prayer deficient because the spiritual X-ray (suwarat descent) cannot penetrate such items — analogous to a medical X-ray requiring the removal of metal objects.

The Sulaymanis combine Zuhr and Asr prayers, and Maghrib and Isha prayers, because the gate for Zuhr remains open for about two and a half hours (overlapping with Asr time) and the gate for Maghrib is very short (15-20 minutes); combining them is therefore valid and practical.

The Prophet designated Ali as his successor at Ghadir Khumm before a crowd of 70,000, declaring 'man kuntu mawlahu fa-hadha 'Aliyyun mawlah' (of whomsoever I am the master, this Ali is his master); the Quranic command 'balligh ma unzila ilayk' compelled this declaration before the Prophet's death.

Abu Talib was the Imam of the time during the Prophet's era; he gave prophethood (nubuwwah) to the Prophet and was a great muwahhid who never worshipped idols — the Islamic world's claim that he died an unbeliever is wrong.

The Da'a'im al-Islam was compiled by Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man on the order of Imam Mu'izz; the Imam certified that this single achievement surpasses all deeds of the mu'minin until the Day of Judgment.

The identity of one's Hajj 'Ali (the highest spiritual superior known only to the Imam) is hidden from everyone; this arrangement prevents unhealthy fixation and ensures followers obey the established rank hierarchy rather than an individual.

Sayyidna Ja'far bin Mansur al-Yaman held the rank of Bab al-Abwab in the era of Imam Mu'izz, though he was unknown in the apparent hierarchy; Qadi al-Nu'man was guided to recognise him as his superior through the Imam's intervention.

The innovation (bid'ah) of tarawih prayer was started in the time of Umar and has no basis in the Prophet's time; bid'ah leads toward misguidance (gumrahi) which leads toward disbelief (kufr) which leads toward hell.
Hujjat has two meanings: (1) a rank below the Imam — Bab al-Abwab and the Imam's Ma'dhun of today are in this rank; (2) the Imam's son designated to succeed him as the next Imam.

Taking the covenant ('ahd) makes one a mustajib, not yet a mu'min; the spiritual birth (ruhani paida'ish) that connects one's nafs-e-natiqah to the chain of the da'wah happens at the moment of the pledge.

The Da'i-e-Mutlaq (absolute missionary) is master of the three jazirahs: Yemen, Hind, and Sindh; only the Da'i of Yemen has authority to appoint mansubs — no mansub can appoint his own successor without the Da'i's order.

The entire cosmic tasbih (glorification) consists of every higher rank lifting the lower rank upward — this is what the moving of beads on a rosary symbolises: the adna (lower) is raised by the a'la (higher).

Today's du'at are in the ranks of Hujjat; compared to du'at of prior eras, present-day Sulaymanis' marasim (venerable figures) have advanced thirty ranks because the era of Qiyamat is near and commanders of high rank are needed.

Salman al-Farsi attained all ten ranks of Bab al-Inbi'ath in the era of Muhammad; the Prophet's statement 'As-Salmanu minna Ahl al-Bayt' means that Salman's babiyyah had ended and he was entering Imamate in his future manifestations.

There are four Du'at-e-Shumuq (highest-ranking du'at of great eminence) recognised in the Sulaymani tradition: Sayyidna Ja'far, Sayyidna Isma'il bin Muhammad, Sayyidna Isma'il bin Hibah, and Ali bin Hibatullah.
The first obligatory question on the Day of Judgement will be about prayer; the face of the entire religion is prayer — nothing takes precedence over it and one who fails to pray cannot be a mu'min.

There are four foundational ranks: nubuwwah (prophethood), risalah (messengership), imamah (imamate), and wasayah (executorship); nubuwwah and risalah are of a lower degree than imamah and wasayah — the ranks of Banu Isra'il prophets are below the Imams of their time who remained hidden.

The Imamate (imamah / laghut / haykal) is distinct from and superior to the Imam himself (nasut); the Imam becomes the Imam only upon receiving the nass (designation) and the bestowing of the haykal from the Bab al-Abwab — until then he is merely the son of the Imam.

The Bab al-Abwab holds the accumulated surat-e-ruhani (spiritual forms) of all mu'minin from the twelve jazirahs; when the Imam performs nass on his son, the Bab al-Abwab transfers this entire deposit to the son, and then immediately must pass away.

The surat-e-ruhani (spiritual form) of a mu'min ascends through each hadd-e-'ali to the da'i, then to the three-island master (da'i-e-mutlaq), then to the Bab al-Abwab, and is refined at each stage before reaching the Imam.

The Imam does not die — he himself brings about his own passing (intiqal) after performing nass on his son and transferring the haykal; this must happen within approximately one to one-and-a-half minutes after nass.

The istihsan-maylan-qisas chain describes how a mu'min falls into spiritual debt: first, appreciating something from another religion (istihsan); second, inclining towards it (maylan); third, actually doing it (qisas) — each step deepens entanglement and prolongs one's stay in this world.

The Hadith 'man tashabbaha bi-qawmin fa-huwa minhum' (whoever imitates a people is from them) means that adopting the religious customs of another community causes one to be resurrected with them on the Day of Judgement.

Things in the physical world fall into three categories from the esoteric perspective: those in an ascending state (halal — permissible) from the nadimin, those in a descending state (haram — forbidden) from the musirrin/mustakbirun, and intermediate things from the mutahayyirin.

One who finishes their qisas (accounts with all creation) is released from rebirth in this world and goes to the hadarat (higher realms of the Imam); qisas continues even for very elevated du'at — only the Imam is ma'sum-e-mutlaq (absolutely infallible) and exempt from qisas.

The seventh Imam in each week is the most superior; when the seventh comes, he absorbs the accumulated spiritual forms (haykal) of the six before him — this is why Friday (jum'ah, meaning 'gathering') follows six days and is the most important.

In the chain of 48 Imams, Imam Tayyib (the 21st) is the master of two weeks (the first and the second) because he absorbed both; similarly, the 35th Imam (at the time of Sayyidna Humam, 1000 years after the Prophet) is called Qaim-e-'Al and is also the master of two weeks.

The 48th Imam is the current Sahib al-'Asr (Master of the Age) and the Hujjat-e-Qaim (representative of the awaited Qaim); recognition of the Imam of one's time is obligatory — 'man mata wa lam ya'rif imama zamanihi, mata mitatan jahiliyyah' (whoever dies without knowing the Imam of his time dies the death of ignorance).
key_terms: man mata wa lam ya'rif imama zamanihi

teaching: Mawlatuna Fatimah is called Umm al-Du'at and held the rank of Hujjat of Ali; the term 'Hujjat' applied to a woman signifies a very high spiritual station in the da'wah hierarchy.

The Ruku' (bowing in prayer) is symbolic evidence (dalil) of the Hujjat and Da'i; the two prostrations (sajdahs) are evidence of the Imam and his Hujjat, and also of 'Minha khalaqnakum wa fiha nu'idukum' — from earth you were created, into it you are returned, from it you will be raised.

The Quran descends from the First Intellect ('Aql-e-Awwal) through intermediaries; the final intermediary who descended upon the Prophet's heart was Mawlana Abu Talib — all previous books (Bible, Torah, Injil) came from the Tenth Intellect.

The Quranic muqatta'at (disjointed letters like 'Alif Lam Mim') have no translation in any language or sect because they are sealed (makhfi); their meanings are found only in the esoteric books of the da'wah.

The Prophet's hadith 'Give the laborer his wage before his sweat dries' has an esoteric meaning: at the moment of death, the dying mu'min is shown a glimpse of his surat-e-ruhani (his accumulated spiritual form / wage) before his breath leaves — and the forms of Mawlana Ali and the Imam of the time are also shown.
key_terms: ya harith hamdan man yamut yarani

teaching: Ali declared: 'Ya Harith Hamdan, man yamut yarani' (O Harith Hamdan, whoever dies sees me) — both believers and unbelievers see Ali at death, the believer with joy and the unbeliever with terror.
key_terms: ya harith hamdan man yamut yarani

teaching: The Prophet's shari'ah is immutable and comprehensive until the Day of Judgement; it is the Sulaymani community that truly follows the Prophet's sunnah — they are therefore the real 'Sunnis' in the meaning of acting on the Prophet's practice.
The Sulaymani era is now in the dawr-e-Qaimi (era of the Qaim), which began about 400 years ago; though people are called the Ummat-e-Muhammadi, the da'wah is now in the period of the Qaim's cycle.

The first perfection (Kamal-e-Awwal) was the state in which all essences in the spiritual world were created equal with knowledge ('ilm), life (hayat), and complete power (qudrah) in a potential state; the second perfection (Kamal-e-Thani) is bringing these qualities into actual expression — the entire world was created so that essences could achieve Kamal-e-Thani.

The nafs-e-natiqah of every Sulaymani is deposited in the Spiritual Kaaba ('alam-e-azal) from the time of the pre-eternal covenant; when one takes the 'ahd on earth for the first time, a spiritual connection (ittisal) is made through the chain from hadd-e-'ali up to the Imam.

The 'ilm-e-ladunni (divinely inspired knowledge of the da'wah) is the most truthful knowledge; after it, the two most accurate sciences are medicine ('ilm al-abdan) and then economics — all other sciences are still 'on the way' and have not reached the destination.

The theory of mabda' and ma'ad in the Sulaymani tradition is not borrowed from Greek philosophy; it has been transmitted since the time of Adam — Aristotle (Arisṭuṭalis) and other Greek philosophers drew from this same tradition because Aristotle himself was a believer in this philosophy.

Sayyidna Muayyad al-Shirazi is the great philosopher of the Sulaymani and Tayyibi da'wah who compiled the doctrines of mabda' and ma'ad; he said if he had lived in the Prophet's time he would have been like Salman al-Farsi.

The natural ascent of matter follows the order: mineral (ma'dan) → plant (nabat) → animal (haywan) → human (insan); descent goes in reverse; this is the divine mill through which all fallen essences gradually progress toward the human form.

Only human flesh from a ritually slaughtered halal animal (on which 'Allahu Akbar' was said) can truly nourish the believer's bodily substance; the act of bismillah during slaughter causes a spiritual chemical change in the animal's substance.

The Sulaymani population worldwide is less than four to five hundred thousand; though small, this community is the real essence of the world — like salt in flour which is small in quantity but gives flavour to the whole.
